title: Parallel Block Decoding Feasibility Analysis
summary: Comprehensive evaluation of parallel DEFLATE block decoding for standard ZIP files. Conclusion: NOT RECOMMENDED for our use case. The combination of (a) few blocks per file, (b) large block sizes, (c) inter-block output dependencies, and (d) inability to detect block boundaries without serial parsing makes parallel block decode infeasible for meaningful speedup on standard DEFLATE streams.

block_structure_empirical_data.methodology: Analyzed all 20 corpus files at compression levels 1, 6, and 9 using a custom block structure analyzer that parses DEFLATE headers and counts blocks, types, decompressed sizes, and literal/backref ratios.

level_6_summary.note: Files with >5 blocks are all incompressible (stored blocks: binary_elf=13, random_bytes=16)

block_types.stored: Only for incompressible data (random_bytes, binary headers)
block_types.fixed_huffman: Zero instances at any compression level

block_sizes.note: zlib creates new blocks at 128KB/256KB boundaries depending on version and settings

challenges_for_parallel_decode.challenge: Block boundary detection requires serial parsing
challenges_for_parallel_decode.description: DEFLATE block boundaries are NOT byte-aligned and cannot be found without decoding the Huffman stream serially. The end-of-block (EOB) symbol is a variable-length Huffman code embedded in the bitstream. To find block N+1, you must decode all of block N.
challenges_for_parallel_decode.implication: Cannot partition work in advance. Must either scan serially or use speculative starting points.
challenges_for_parallel_decode.comparison: GDeflate solves this by reformatting: each block starts at a known byte offset. But this requires a custom compression format, incompatible with standard ZIP.

challenges_for_parallel_decode.description: Back-references can span block boundaries: a match in block N can reference data written in block N-1 (up to 32KB back). This means block N's output depends on block N-1's final 32KB. Blocks cannot be decoded in isolation.
challenges_for_parallel_decode.implication: Even if we could find block boundaries, blocks need the tail of the previous block's output. Could be handled by pre-copying the 32KB overlap, but adds complexity.
challenges_for_parallel_decode.comparison: GDeflate uses independently decodable blocks with no cross-block references.

challenges_for_parallel_decode.challenge: Too few blocks for meaningful parallelism
challenges_for_parallel_decode.description: 50% of our corpus files (10/20) have exactly 1 compressed block. 75% (15/20) have ≤2 blocks. Even text_1024k (1MB) has only 5 blocks. Maximum parallelism for typical files is 1-2 threads.
challenges_for_parallel_decode.implication: Thread creation/synchronization overhead likely exceeds the benefit for 1-2 blocks. Even with 5 blocks, Amdahl's law limits speedup to ~2-3x at best.

challenges_for_parallel_decode.description: Block sizes vary significantly even within a single file. For english_prose L6: blocks are 180KB and 81KB — a 2.2:1 ratio. This means the larger block dominates execution time.
challenges_for_parallel_decode.implication: Load imbalance limits parallelism. The critical path is the largest block.

challenges_for_parallel_decode.description: For files <256KB (most of our corpus), the single-block decode time is ~100-500 microseconds. Thread creation/synchronization overhead on Linux is ~10-50 microseconds, which is 5-50% of total decode time.
challenges_for_parallel_decode.implication: Only beneficial for large files (>512KB) with multiple blocks.

approaches_evaluated.name: Multi-threaded block decode
approaches_evaluated.description: Scan for block boundaries serially (fast, since we just need to find EOB), then decode blocks in parallel on separate threads.
approaches_evaluated.reason: Block boundary scanning IS decoding. You can't find the EOB without decoding all preceding symbols. Also, only 1-5 blocks per file.

approaches_evaluated.name: Speculative parallel start
approaches_evaluated.description: Start decoding at estimated block boundaries (e.g., every N bytes). If we guess wrong, discard and retry.
approaches_evaluated.reason: DEFLATE has no byte-aligned sync points. A wrong starting bit position will produce invalid Huffman codes, but detecting invalidity may take many symbols. The retry overhead is prohibitive.

approaches_evaluated.name: GDeflate-style reformatting
approaches_evaluated.description: During compression, output independently decodable blocks with explicit byte-aligned boundaries. Compatible with DEFLATE syntax but not with existing compressors.
approaches_evaluated.reason: Requires controlling the compressor. Not compatible with standard ZIP files produced by other tools. This is the GDeflate/GPU approach.

approaches_evaluated.name: Pipeline parallelism
approaches_evaluated.description: Overlap block N's match copying with block N+1's Huffman decoding. The Huffman decode output goes to a staging buffer, then the match copy uses the output buffer.
approaches_evaluated.reason: Match copy and Huffman decode are interleaved (every match copy happens between Huffman decodes). Can't cleanly separate them into pipeline stages.

gdeflate.approach: Custom compression format that splits data into independently decodable 64KB tiles. Each tile has its own Huffman tables and no cross-tile references.
gdeflate.speedup: 10-40x over CPU zlib via GPU parallelism
gdeflate.applicability: NOT applicable to standard ZIP files. Requires custom compressor.

pugz.approach: Parallel decompression of gzip streams by scanning for sync points (block boundaries that happen to align on byte boundaries + known fixed-Huffman patterns).
pugz.applicability: Only works with certain compressor outputs (gzip with sync markers). Not general for arbitrary DEFLATE streams.

isal_multithread.approach: ISA-L provides a multi-threaded decompression API for large buffers, splitting at stored block boundaries or using speculative sync.
isal_multithread.applicability: Only effective for files with stored block markers. Not applicable to fully compressed DEFLATE.

recommendation_rationale: 50% of corpus files have only 1 block — zero parallelism available.
Block boundaries cannot be detected without serial decoding.
Inter-block LZ77 dependencies prevent independent block decode.
Threading overhead dominates for small/medium files (<512KB).
All viable parallel approaches require either format modification (GDeflate) or special compressor output (pugz).
Our focus should remain on maximizing single-stream throughput, where the packed entry optimization has been highly effective.
alternative_recommendation: Focus remaining effort on: (1) further hot-path micro-optimization, (2) PGO builds for deployment, (3) comprehensive evaluation and documentation.
